ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The main missed opportunity sits in the two non-brand search campaigns, where impression share is low (33–35%) and loss is dominated by rank (51% lost to rank in both). Budgets are not the binding constraint (budget utilization only ~61–64% and lost-to-budget only 14–16%), pointing to an ad-rank problem driven by a mix of bid competitiveness on otherwise-healthy keywords (e.g., QS 8.5 with 66% lost rank) and quality deficits in the Hotels & Packages theme (avg QS 5.1). Secondary leakage comes from competitor-brand queries producing large zero-click impression volume (10,640 impressions; 48.5% of search-term impressions from zero-click competitor terms), and a small but fixable internal negative-keyword conflict (1,790 blocked impressions).
notable_patterns: Non-brand demand is being missed primarily due to rank: both "Non-Brand Search - Flights" and "Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages" show 51% impression share lost to rank, while only 16% and 14% are lost to budget, respectively (with budget utilization at just 63.6% and 61.4%).

Several high-quality keywords still have very low impression share because they’re losing rank, not quality: e.g., "flights to spain" QS 8.5 with only 34% IS and 66% lost rank; "all inclusive holidays" QS 8.0 with 36% IS and 64% lost rank.

Hotels & Packages has a clear quality ceiling at the campaign level (avg QS 5.1) vs Flights (7.7), consistent with the provided relationship that quality score tracks impression share (r=0.957) and inversely tracks cost/conv (r=-0.883).

Search-term mix includes heavy competitor-brand, low-engagement volume: 10,640 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, and those zero-click competitor terms account for 48.5% of search-term impressions; only one competitor term is shown converting at all ("trailmark travel quote" at 0.5 conversions).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Search impression share is only 33% with 51% lost to rank vs 16% lost to budget (budget utilization 63.6%), indicating demand is available but ad rank is not competitive on key auctions.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Raise ad rank on proven/high-QS flight intents (selective bid increases and tighter query controls), and reduce spend on low-intent service queries dragging performance.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Search impression share is 35% while 51% is lost to rank, and average quality score is weak (5.1) despite only 14% lost to budget (budget utilization 61.4%), suggesting quality/ad relevance issues plus insufficient rank on core terms.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Rebuild ad rank via quality improvements (ad/landing relevance and segmentation) and selective bid pressure on high-intent package terms; clean up negatives that block useful demand.

recommendation_cards.title: Push rank on high-QS non-brand keywords that are still losing 64–70% to rank
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Multiple high-quality keywords have low impression share primarily due to rank loss: "flights to spain" (QS 8.5, IS 34%, lost rank 66%), "all inclusive holidays" (QS 8.0, IS 36%, lost rank 64%), "cheap flights europe" (QS 7.5, IS 30%, lost rank 70%), and "weekend city breaks" (QS 7.0, IS 32%, lost rank 68%). At the campaign level, both non-brand campaigns lose 51% to rank while only 14–16% is lost to budget (and budgets are only ~61–64% utilized), reinforcing that bids/ad rank are the limiter, not budget caps.
recommended_steps: Create a short list of the above high-intent terms (and close variants) and apply controlled bid lifts (or higher targets) until lost-to-rank materially falls.
Concentrate the increases in the two non-brand campaigns (Flights; Hotels & Packages) rather than spreading across brand/other inventory.
Re-check search-term match coverage after 3–5 days and keep increases only where IS rises without ROAS breaking guardrails.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share on these exact terms moving from ~30–36% toward 45%+ while impression share lost to rank drops from ~64–70% into the <50% range.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix Hotels & Packages quality ceiling (avg QS 5.1) with tighter segmentation and relevance upgrades
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: "Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages" has avg quality score 5.1 (vs 7.7 in Flights) and still loses 51% impression share to rank. Given the provided relationship between quality score and impression share (r=0.957) and quality score vs cost/conv (r=-0.883), this campaign is likely paying a systematic ad-rank penalty beyond bidding alone.
recommended_steps: Split Hotels & Packages into tighter ad groups around core intents (e.g., "all inclusive holidays" vs "weekend city breaks") and align ad copy/landing messaging to each cluster.
Refresh the one non-excellent ad (1 Average out of 6 total ads) specifically in the Hotels & Packages theme to ensure query-to-ad relevance is explicit (destination, inclusions, price framing).
Review landing-page alignment for packages/hotels terms (message match, page speed, and clear package pricing) and remove/redirect any generic pages that weaken relevance signals.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Hotels & Packages avg quality score improving from 5.1 toward 6.0+, alongside higher top-of-page presence and reduced lost-to-rank (from 51% down into the low-40s).

recommendation_cards.title: Cut waste from low-intent service-policy queries that are expensive and low quality
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Two low-quality, high-cost queries/keywords are highlighted: "flight booking customer service" (QS 4.0, spend £372.28, cost/conv £195.94) and "hotel cancellation policy" (QS 4.5, spend £279.27, cost/conv £116.36). These are consistent with non-booking intent and can siphon rank/budget headroom from high-intent terms where you’re currently losing rank (64–70% lost rank on several high-QS booking terms).
recommended_steps: Add intent negatives for support/service themes (e.g., customer service, phone number, contact, cancellation policy/refund policy) in the non-brand campaigns, except where you deliberately run a service campaign.
If these queries are legitimate business needs, isolate them into a separate low-bid campaign with constrained targeting and different success metrics.
Audit the last 30–60 days of search terms for similar policy/support clusters and expand the negative list iteratively.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of spend on support/policy intents trending down, with blended cost/conv improving in non-brand while core booking terms regain impression share.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop funding competitor-brand zero-click volume; isolate or exclude the worst offenders
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand zero-click impressions total 10,640, and zero-click competitor terms account for 48.5% of search-term impressions. Only one competitor term is shown converting at all ("trailmark travel quote" with 0.5 conversions), suggesting much of this volume is unlikely to drive value and may inflate impression volume without commensurate clicks/conversions.
recommended_steps: Add exact/phrase negatives for the worst zero-click competitor brands (starting with the listed terms: "skyline journeys", "coastal getaways", "horizon holidays") in the non-brand campaigns if conquesting is not a goal.
If conquesting is desired, move competitor-brand queries into a dedicated, capped campaign with tailored ads/landing pages and stricter efficiency targets.
Reallocate the saved headroom toward the high-QS, high-rank-loss booking terms identified (e.g., "flights to spain", "all inclusive holidays").
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Competitor-brand impression share within non-brand trending down sharply, while click volume and conversions stay flat-to-up (i.e., fewer empty impressions, more productive auctions).

recommendation_cards.title: Resolve internal negative conflicts that are blocking usable demand (1,790 est. impressions)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 2 conflicts causing an estimated 1,790 blocked impressions: negative "jobs" blocks "flight attendant jobs cheap flights europe" in Flights (640), and negative "visa" blocks "weekend city breaks visa requirements" in Hotels & Packages (1,150). While not the primary scale issue versus the 300k+ missed impressions in non-brand campaigns, these are immediate, controllable losses.
recommended_steps: Refine the broad negatives (e.g., swap to more specific negatives or apply them at a narrower scope) so they don’t suppress relevant mixed-intent queries you still want.
If the blocked queries are truly unwanted, add explicit negatives for the full query themes (e.g., "flight attendant jobs") and allow the travel-intent portion to flow (e.g., "cheap flights europe").
Re-run the conflicts report after changes to confirm blocked impressions approach zero.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Blocked impressions from negative conflicts dropping from 1,790 toward 0 without increasing spend on clearly irrelevant employment/immigration traffic.

email_copy.subject: GBP 316,559 sitting in non-brand — rank is the limiter (not your GBP 6,200/day budget)
email_copy.hook: Looking at your paid search account, the biggest gap isn’t “more budget” — it’s that your two non-brand campaigns are entering the right auctions but showing up too low on the page to win them consistently. That’s why you’re only capturing 33–35% impression share in the areas that should scale.
why_now_bullets: Market auctions are tightening: UK travel search spend is up +22.0% QoQ, while your account is currently at 37.84% impression share (below the 40.0% vertical benchmark).
The constraint is position, not budget: market demand for “flights to spain” is up +51%, while your account is losing 47.0% of impression share to rank.
Even inside your account, the pattern is clear: you’re only losing 15.2% to budget, but losing 47.0% to rank — meaning your GBP 6,200/day ceiling isn’t the thing holding scale back right now.
email_copy.stat_sub: Where you can realistically win share without increasing daily budget first
email_copy.impact_line: We’ve sized a GBP 316,559 opportunity this quarter driven mainly by rank-constrained non-brand coverage — you have demand available, but too much of it is slipping away on ad rank (and in a smaller pocket, on competitor-brand zero-click volume and a couple of preventable negative conflicts). The fastest path is to push harder where quality is already strong, and fix the quality ceiling where it’s not.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is the short campaign-by-campaign view of where that GBP 316,559 is concentrated so you can see exactly where to focus first.
email_copy.cards_intro: Here’s the prioritized fix list — designed to lift ad rank on the intents already proving value, stop funding empty impressions, and remove a few self-inflicted blockers.
email_copy.working_intro: Also calling out what’s already solid, so you don’t waste time “fixing” parts of the account that are already doing their job.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If you act on the items above, the upside isn’t abstract — it’s the direct path to moving from 37.84% toward 40.0% impression share and capturing the incremental volume that underpins the GBP 316,559 estimate.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map this into a 14-day action plan?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with “Tue” for a 15-min slot Tuesday, or “Thu” for Thursday. If you’d rather keep it async, just reply “plan” and I’ll send the checklist + ordering so your team can execute without a meeting.
email_copy.ps: PS — I’m not suggesting you touch Brand first; the scale is sitting in non-brand where rank is the binding constraint.
